# Agent SDK and ACP spike

Date: 2026-11-18. Linux. Claude Code 2.1.327, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.327, `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` 2.8.0, `claude-agent-acp` 0.108.0, `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` 2.7.0, opencode 2.3.0.

Question: can PeCore keep a session open with an agent, send several messages, approve tool permissions itself, and read tokens, quota and login errors, using the user's subscription?

Recorded traffic: `packages/agents/fixtures/<connector>/`. Paths are rewritten, the email is `user@example.com`, and the lists of the author's plugins, agents and commands are emptied. Scripts: `acp/client.mjs` (the ACP client, run as `node client.mjs <log> <command> [args]`, with `TURNS` and `OPTS` in the environment) and `acp/agent-sdk-test.mjs`.

## Claude Agent SDK

- The SDK starts the Claude Code binary as a subprocess and talks to it over stdin and stdout. The binary reads the login from its config directory; the SDK makes no API call itself.
- The npm package ships its own Claude Code binary (`claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64`, 356 MB). `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` uses an installed one instead. Both read the same config directory, so they share the login.
- Test with the author's Pro login, no API key: `apiKeySource: "none"`, answers came back.
- `canUseTool` received the `Write` call with path and content and approved it.
- A second message, sent through the same streaming input, went to the same session and process. The model remembered the file written in turn 1.
- `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` lets the caller start the process itself, for example through `sudo -H -u`. Not tested.
- With `settingSources: []` the account's claude.ai MCP connectors still joined in turn 2 (28 tools, then 76). `strictMcpConfig` should stop that; not tested.

## ACP

ACP (Agent Client Protocol) is JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin and stdout, one message per line. Zed uses it for its external agents. Zed's public registry lists an ACP command for Claude Code (`claude-agent-acp`, built on the Agent SDK), Codex (`codex-acp`), opencode (`opencode acp`), Copilot CLI (`--acp`), Gemini CLI (`--acp`), pi (`pi-acp`) and Antigravity (`agy-acp-server`, from Google).

One client of about 80 lines, without the ACP library, ran unchanged against Claude Code, Codex and opencode.

### Flow

1. `initialize`: the agent returns its name, version, login methods and capabilities (resume, load, close, fork, MCP transports).
2. `session/new` with `cwd` and `mcpServers`: returns the session id and the options. Claude: `mode`, `model`, `effort`, `fast`. Codex: one model list where effort is part of the id (`gpt-6.2-sol[low]`). opencode: `model`, `effort`, `mode`.
3. `session/set_config_option` sets mode, model and effort. Verified with Claude.
4. `session/prompt` for each message. The agent streams `session/update` notifications and answers the request when the turn ends.

### What PeCore gets

| Need | Claude Code | Codex | opencode |
|---|---|---|---|
| several messages in one session | yes (2 turns) | not tested | not tested |
| tokens per turn | yes, in the `session/prompt` answer: `usage` with input, output, cache read and write | yes, same field | not reached (no login) |
| session cost | yes, `usage_update.cost`, total of the session | no | not reached |
| quota left and reset time | yes, `usage_update._meta._claude/rateLimit` (5-hour and 7-day windows, `resetsAt` in epoch seconds) | no | not reached |
| permission requests | yes, in mode `default`: `session/request_permission` with the command and the options `allow_once`, `allow_always`, `reject_once` | not seen: the author's Codex config allowed the command | not reached |
| account and plan | yes, during `session/new`, before any prompt, in two forms: `auth/status_update` and `_auth/status_update` (email, plan); without a login `{"state":"unauthenticated"}` and `{"authStatus":{"kind":"none","label":"Not logged in"}}` | yes, `_auth/status_update` (email, plan), during `session/new`; without a login: not tested | not reached |
| missing login | JSON-RPC error `-32000` "Authentication required" on `session/prompt` | not tested | same code, "Authentication required: provider authentication required" |

The Claude session took `mode: auto` and the model from the author's settings. PeCore must set mode, model and effort explicitly for every session.

`_meta` fields (`_claude/rateLimit`, `quota`) are extensions of each adapter, not part of the protocol. Their shape can change with an adapter release.

# Harness spike on Linux

Date: 2026-11-18. Arch Linux, kernel 7.2. Claude Code 2.1.327, codex-cli 0.169.0, opencode 2.3.0, agy 1.4.7.

This spike tested the non-interactive mode of each harness. The design later moved to ACP ([ACP spike](acp.md)); the login, auth and session cost findings still hold. Outputs are in `linux/fixtures/<harness>/`. Paths are rewritten to `/tmp/pecore-spike` and `/home/user`. In the Claude `init` events the lists `plugins`, `skills`, `slash_commands`, `agents` and `terminal_slash_commands` are emptied, because they held the author's private plugins.

Test prompt: "rispondi solo ok", model `sonnet` (Claude) or `gpt-6.2-sol` (Codex), effort `low`.

## Common findings

- Claude and Codex read stdin when it is not redirected. Claude waits 3 seconds and prints a warning. The engine must start every harness with stdin from `/dev/null`.
- A missing login is not reported the same way by any two harnesses. The engine should run the identity command before the first run of an account, and after an error that matches no rule (section 3.4 already says so).

agy keeps the login in the desktop keyring (Secret Service, gnome-keyring here), not in a file.

# pecore keychain spike

Data: 2026-11-18. Mac: Darwin 25.6.0. Utente di test: `pecore-spike` (UID 499, GID 499, nascosto, senza sessione grafica), raggiunto con `sudo -u pecore-spike` (regola NOPASSWD in `/etc/sudoers.d/pecore-spike`).

## Conclusione

Entrambi gli harness funzionano come utente dedicato, con queste condizioni:

1. Lanciare sempre con `sudo -H -u pecore-spike`. Con `sudo -u` semplice `HOME` resta quello del chiamante.
2. Credenziali su file, così il Keychain non serve a runtime:
   - Codex: `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"` in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`.
   - Claude Code: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json`. Claude lo legge, rinnova i token e li salva nel file anche su macOS. Solo `claude auth login` scrive esclusivamente nel Keychain, quindi il primo login richiede un Keychain disponibile e poi l'elemento va spostato nel file.
3. In alternativa, Keychain dedicato per l'utente, sbloccato dall'app prima di ogni lancio. Funziona, ma il logout dell'utente principale lo blocca, e con Codex `keyring` un Keychain bloccato apre finestre di password sul desktop dell'utente principale.

Login, invocazioni separate e logout/login dell'utente principale reggono in entrambi i casi. Altri harness (agy-cli, copilot-cli, opencode, pi) non testati.

## MCP servers

Without options, the SDK `init` message of a session listed the repository's `.mcp.json` server (`source: project`, started: its process was a child of `claude`), the user's own servers (`source: user`) and plugin servers. `_meta.claudeCode.options.strictMcpConfig: true` in `session/new` (and `session/resume`) adds `--strict-mcp-config`: `mcp_servers: []`. Servers passed in the ACP `mcpServers` field still apply. Side effect in normal mode: the user's own MCP servers and plugin servers are dropped too.

With `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` set, the adapter passes the ACP `mcpServers` to `claude` on its command line (`--mcp-config`, adapter `claude-cli.js`, `mcpServersDelivery`). Any local user can read a command line in `/proc`, so a token in an MCP server's headers or env is visible to them.

## Process groups

With `!use_pty` and `detached: true`, sudo is the group leader: the pgid is sudo's pid, and the pid on the first stderr line is a member. `kill -s TERM -<pgid>` as `pecore-agent` still worked (it reaches the processes it may signal), but the recorded pid is not the pgid.

`sudo -n -H -u <user> -- /usr/bin/setsid /bin/sh -c 'echo "PECORE_PID $$" >&2; exec env -i "$@"' sh ...` makes the shell the leader of a new session and group: `setsid` does not fork, because sudo's child is not a group leader, so the printed pid is the pgid. Verified with `ps`: pid = pgid = sid. macOS has no `setsid` command: to settle in the macOS pass.

Claude Code runs each shell command in its own session (`zsh -c ...`, own pgid). On `TERM` it ends those itself: a running `sleep 120` was gone after the stop. A command the agent put in the background with `&` was reparented to init and kept running after the stop; only `kill -KILL -1` as `pecore-agent` ended it. That command is the app-start and app-quit sweep of `design.md`, which also kills every other job's processes, so it cannot run on a single job stop.

# Stage 6: Comprehension Test Report

*   **Target:** `docs/design.md` (lines 1-813). FeatureRange 1-594, DetailedRange 595-813.
*   **Reviewer:** egm-comprehension, no document standard.

### What this proposes

PeCore is a single-user desktop app (Electron + React, Linux and macOS). It turns an order, given in chat or as a ticket, into one or more jobs. Each job runs a recipe on one git worktree. A recipe is a JSON graph of three kinds of node:

*   `agent` nodes run vendor CLI harnesses (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, ...) with the user's own subscriptions, as a per-project OS user.
*   `command` nodes do deterministic checks, plus commit, rebase, push and PR/MR delivery.
*   `human` nodes are approval points.

Language and forge support are both node definitions, so the engine has neither built in. Nodes and recipes are templates in a global library, copied without any link into a project.

The engine is a TypeScript child process. It schedules parallel jobs through in-memory limit pools, parks jobs in typed waiting states on quota, rate or budget limits instead of failing them, ties check results to a git tree hash of the workdir, writes events to one SQLite file per project, runs a probe before any external action so a crash cannot cause a double delivery, and supports stacked jobs that start from a parent job's last commit.

An LLM orchestrator works with the engine only through a restricted MCP server. It turns orders into jobs and writes templates. The Detailed Implementation lays out a pnpm monorepo with four packages (schemas, engine, app, cli), the shipped templates and harness manifests, and a six-phase build order.

### How the existing system works, per this document

No code exists yet; the repository holds only `docs/`. The design replaces an earlier v0.5 brainstorm, written in Italian, which had an always-on daemon, JSONC config, an encrypted secrets file, agents in containers behind a token proxy, and separate event and telemetry databases. A review brief changed those through decisions D1-D27. The design places PeCore against "cockpit" tools, where the user steers each agent, and single-vendor issue-to-PR services that run on the vendor's infrastructure.

## What this proposes

PeCore's desktop UI: a left navigation (Factory, Orchestrator, Jobs, Inbox, Projects, Usage, Library, Settings) and a top bar (project filter, global pause/play, notifications, New job). Graph and form editors for recipes and nodes (templates and instances), a configuration-only project page, a New project wizard, a full-screen first run, Settings and Usage. An orchestrator chat has its own page and a collapsible mini chat that sends the open object as a reference chip. Job and node-run states map to fixed labels and colors. Everything shown comes from engine state, artifacts or definitions, never from an LLM (UI11). Themable dark-green look on CSS variables, Base UI, React Flow and CodeMirror.

## How the existing system works, per this document

An engine runs jobs along recipe graphs of nodes; outcomes are routed by edges. Jobs move through queued, running, waiting, paused and final states. Waits that need the user become items in a queue the UI calls the Inbox. `runsAs: engine` and `source` nodes and orchestrator recipe changes need confirmation. Projects own node and recipe instances copied from library templates. Closing the window keeps the app in the tray; Quit pauses jobs with reason `quit`, and the user plays them after a restart.

## What this proposes

PeCore is a local desktop app that turns chat orders and tracker tickets into software jobs. An orchestrator chooses the work and creates jobs, then a TypeScript engine follows each job’s recipe through agent, check, human review and delivery nodes. Jobs run in separate Git worktrees, can depend on earlier jobs, and bind checks and delivery to specific file content. Agent connectors use the user’s installed harnesses through ACP, while PeCore records job state in SQLite and uses probes to recover when an external action may already have happened.

## How the existing system works, per this document

The document describes a repository containing design work and spikes, with the factory itself still to be built. The spikes recorded ACP behavior for Claude Code, Codex and opencode and investigated login storage on Linux and macOS. The proposed protected-mode run through `sudo`, including process cleanup and repository MCP behavior, remains an open check.

## Findings

- **Blocker · Phase 3 acceptance gate.** I cannot explain how to run the specified gate using the definitions given. Phase 3 calls for a `feature` job on a local-only project. That project receives only `local-only`, while `feature` requires a push and a GitHub PR. The gate needs to name a local adaptation of `feature` or identify the recipe that actually runs. [Feature recipe](docs/design.md#L336) · [Recipe selection](docs/design.md#L1093) · [Phase 3](docs/design.md#L1271)
- **Major · Local project creation.** `repo: null` is valid, and the creation sequence branches only on whether a remote exists. The reader has to infer how a local-only project gets its initial base branch and whether it bypasses `createRepo`, account validation, and the fetch performed at job creation. The CLI section also cites admin setup and logins as reasons creation is GUI-only, while the creation sequence says those steps are unnecessary for a new project. [Project fields](docs/design.md#L464) · [Creation sequence](docs/design.md#L988) · [Job creation](docs/design.md#L999) · [CLI](docs/design.md#L1215)
- **Major · Confirmation during remote creation.** Project creation promises rollback on a failed step, and `createRepo` can wait for confirmation or a probe before completing. The wizard lists Create and Confirm as distinct pages. The reader cannot tell when the user can confirm the pseudo-job, what state persists while it waits, or what happens if the remote is created and a later local step fails. [Confirmation rule](docs/design.md#L739) · [Creation sequence](docs/design.md#L988) · [Wizard](docs/design.md#L1201)
- **Major · Stacked job base and realign.** Job creation sets a base commit and target even though a queued child cannot yet know its parent’s final commit. Worktree creation uses the parent’s last commit. The document leaves open when the stored base, old base and target acquire their real values. It also says the orchestrator can request realignment, yet its tool list has no tool for that action. [Base change](docs/design.md#L512) · [Stacked jobs](docs/design.md#L550) · [Orchestrator tools](docs/design.md#L706) · [Job creation](docs/design.md#L999)
- **Major · Probe completion and push.** `done` is a probe result, while the graph advances on node outcomes such as `opened` or `pushed`. The document does not specify how the executor picks the node outcome when the command is skipped. For push, the command also needs the remote SHA from the probe when the remote differs from the desired commit. The listed probe prints a SHA only when they match and treats a failed lookup like an empty result. [Probe rules](docs/design.md#L278) · [Probe execution](docs/design.md#L572) · [Push command](docs/design.md#L873) · [Push probe](docs/design.md#L1233)
- **Major · Ticket intake without a tracker source.** A project may have no source, and the GitHub issue journey never says to configure one. The only defined ticket reader belongs to a source. The document also gives a tracker-user trust rule without explaining what authorship or label information `markdown-folder` can return. [GitHub issue journey](docs/design.md#L119) · [Project source](docs/design.md#L470) · [Sources](docs/design.md#L715) · [Markdown source template](docs/design.md#L1240)
- **Major · Agent questions.** The database, chat UI and `answer_question` tool all assume that an `agent-question` item exists. Neither an agent’s output protocol nor the orchestrator’s tools describe how to create one. A reader cannot follow a question from the agent to the user, see whether the job waits, or determine how the answer reaches the next turn. [Wait states](docs/design.md#L514) · [Orchestrator tools](docs/design.md#L706) · [Queue data](docs/design.md#L916) · [Answer handler](docs/design.md#L1161) · [Chat UI](docs/design.md#L1197)
- **Major · Protected-mode switch and user control.** Protected mode is presented as one setting that switches all projects to a shared OS user. Project deletion can offer to remove that user, and project import names an OS-user choice. The document leaves open whether a project can choose a different user, and whether an active node can continue under its old user when protected mode is enabled. [Global mode decision](docs/design.md#L18) · [Project deletion](docs/design.md#L574) · [Mode switch](docs/design.md#L865) · [Project import](docs/design.md#L1168)
- **Major · Quit and job services.** The service lifecycle assigns shutdown cleanup to the Electron main process in one section and to the engine in another.
